questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A catchment has annual rainfall $P=800\,\text{mm}$, evapotranspiration $ET=500\,\text{mm}$, and groundwater recharge $G=80\,\text{mm}$. The surface runoff $R$ (in mm) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Water balance: $P = R + ET + G$.

**Working.**
$$R = P - ET - G = 800 - 500 - 80 = 220.$$

**Answer.** $220\,\text{mm}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $12\,\text{km}^2$ urban catchment receives $25\,\text{mm}$ of rainfall. If the runoff coefficient $C=0.6$, the runoff volume (in $\text{m}^3$) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Using the rational method $Q=CiA$, a catchment of area $5\,\text{km}^2$ has runoff coefficient $C=0.5$ and rainfall intensity $i=20\,\text{mm/h}$. The peak discharge $Q$ (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Horton's infiltration capacity is $f_p = f_c + (f_0 - f_c)e^{-kt}$ with $f_0=80\,\text{mm/h}$, $f_c=10\,\text{mm/h}$, $k=2\,\text{h}^{-1}$. The total infiltration (in mm) over $3$ hours is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $2$-h unit hydrograph has ordinates $(0, 5, 20, 35, 25, 15, 5, 0)\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ at $0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14$ hours. The peak of the $S$-hydrograph (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** The $S$-hydrograph is the cumulative sum of unit hydrograph ordinates at time interval $D$ (here $D=2$ h), then scaled by $3600/D$.

**Working.**
The sum of all UH ordinates = $0+5+20+35+25+15+5+0 = 105$.
$$S_{\text{peak}} = 105 \times \frac{3600}{2 \times 3600} = 52.5.$$

**Answer.** $52.5\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.stem: Flood data for a river: mean $\bar{x}=2500\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, standard deviation $s=800\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, and the reduced mean $\bar{y}_N=0.5772$ and reduced standard deviation $\sigma_N=1.2825$ for $N=25$ years. The $100$-year flood (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) by Gumbel's method is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Penman's equation gives net radiation $R_n=5.5\,\text{mm/d}$, aerodynamic term $=3.2\,\text{mm/d}$, and psychrometric ratio $\gamma=0.66\,\text{mbar/}^\circ\text{C}$ with $\Delta=1.8\,\text{mbar/}^\circ\text{C}$. The potential evapotranspiration (in mm/d) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A stream rating curve is $Q = 25 H^{1.5}$, where $Q$ is in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ and $H$ is gauge height in m. If the gauge reads $H=4\,\text{m}$, the discharge $Q$ (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Direct substitution into the rating curve equation.

**Working.**
$$Q = 25\times(4)^{1.5} = 25\times8 = 200.$$

**Answer.** $200\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $15\,\text{km}^2$ catchment has $P=120\,\text{mm}$, infiltration $=55\,\text{mm}$, evaporation $=25\,\text{mm}$, and deep percolation $=10\,\text{mm}$. The runoff coefficient $C$ is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A storm of $6\,\text{cm}$ excess rainfall in $4$ hours produces a direct runoff hydrograph with peak $=120\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$. The peak ordinate of the $4$-h unit hydrograph (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Unit hydrograph peak = (DRH peak) / (excess rainfall depth in cm).

**Working.**
$$q_p = \frac{120}{6} = 20.$$

**Answer.** $20\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Annual maximum flood data: $\overline{\log Q}=3.4$, $\sigma_{\log Q}=0.3$, skew coefficient $C_s=1.0$. For $T=50$ years, the frequency factor $K_{50}$ (by log-Pearson Type III tables) $=1.88$. The $50$-year flood $Q_{50}$ (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Log-Pearson Type III: $\log Q_T = \overline{\log Q} + K_T \cdot \sigma_{\log Q}$.

**Working.**
$$\log Q_{50} = 3.4 + 1.88\times0.3 = 3.4 + 0.564 = 3.964.$$
$$Q_{50} = 10^{3.964} = 9215.$$

**Answer.** $9215\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A lake has surface area $2\,\text{km}^2$. Inflow $=1.5\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, outflow $=1.2\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, precipitation $=2\,\text{mm/d}$, evaporation $=3\,\text{mm/d}$. The change in storage (in mm/d) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Thornthwaite's formula gives $ET_p = 1.6 \left(\dfrac{10\,T_I}{I}\right)^a$ where the heat index $I=3.2$ and exponent $a=0.58$. For mean monthly temperature $=20^\circ\text{C}$, $ET_p$ (in mm/month) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $2$-h unit hydrograph has a peak of $30\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$. A storm produces excess rainfall of $3\,\text{cm}$ in the 1st hour and $5\,\text{cm}$ in the 2nd hour. The peak discharge (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) of the resulting DRH is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Convolve excess rainfall with unit hydrograph: DRH peak = $\sum (P_i \times q_{\text{peak}})$ considering lag.

**Working.**
$$\text{Peak} = 3\times30 + 5\times30 = 240.$$

**Answer.** $240\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A stream cross-section is divided into $3$ subsections. Subsection data: $A_1=10\,\text{m}^2$, $v_1=0.5\,\text{m/s}$; $A_2=15\,\text{m}^2$, $v_2=0.8\,\text{m/s}$; $A_3=8\,\text{m}^2$, $v_3=0.4\,\text{m/s}$. The total discharge (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.

questions.stem: Horton's equation: $f_p = 20 + 40e^{-1.5t}$ (mm/h). The time (in minutes) when infiltration capacity drops to $30\,\text{mm/h}$ is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $6$-h unit hydrograph has a time base of $48$ hours and peak discharge $=50\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$. The area of the catchment (in $\text{km}^2$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** 1 cm excess rainfall over catchment area = volume under UH. Area $= \dfrac{\text{Volume under UH}}{0.01\,\text{m}}$.

**Working.**
Approximate volume by triangular approximation: $V = \frac{1}{2}\times48\times3600\times50 = 4{,}320{,}000\,\text{m}^3$.
$$A = \frac{4{,}320{,}000}{0.01} = 432\times10^6\,\text{m}^2 = 432\,\text{km}^2.$$

**Answer.** $432\,\text{km}^2$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A confined aquifer has thickness $b=30\,\text{m}$ and hydraulic conductivity $K=15\,\text{m/d}$. The transmissivity $T$ (in $\text{m}^2/\text{d}$) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A well in a confined aquifer ($T=500\,\text{m}^2/\text{d}$, $S=5\times10^{-4}$) pumps at $Q=2000\,\text{m}^3/\text{d}$. At $r=100\,\text{m}$ and $t=10\,\text{days}$, the drawdown $s$ (in m) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Cooper-Jacob semi-log method: drawdown $= 2\,\text{m}$ at $t=100\,\text{min}$ and $= 4\,\text{m}$ at $t=1000\,\text{min}$. The transmissivity $T$ (in $\text{m}^2/\text{d}$) for $Q=500\,\text{m}^3/\text{d}$ is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Cooper-Jacob: $\Delta s = \dfrac{2.303Q}{4\pi T}$ per log cycle.

**Working.**
$$\Delta s = 4 - 2 = 2\,\text{m}.$$
$$T = \frac{2.303Q}{4\pi\Delta s} = \frac{2.303\times500}{4\pi\times2} = \frac{1151.5}{25.13} = 45.8\,\text{m}^2/\text{d}.$$

**Answer.** $45.8\,\text{m}^2/\text{d}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Steady flow to a well in a confined aquifer: $h_1=25\,\text{m}$ at $r_1=50\,\text{m}$, $h_2=22\,\text{m}$ at $r_2=200\,\text{m}$, aquifer thickness $b=20\,\text{m}$. The hydraulic conductivity $K$ (in m/d) for $Q=300\,\text{m}^3/\text{d}$ is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A confined aquifer has storativity $S=5\times10^{-4}$, porosity $n=0.3$, and thickness $b=25\,\text{m}$. A pressure drop of $10\,\text{m}$ of head occurs. The volume of water released per unit area (in m) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** For confined aquifers, $S = S_s b$ where $S_s = \rho g(\alpha + n\beta)$. Water released per unit area $= S \times \Delta h$.

**Working.**
$$\text{Volume per unit area} = S \times \Delta h = 5\times10^{-4}\times10 = 0.005\,\text{m}.$$

**Answer.** $0.005\,\text{m}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A flow net has $N_f=5$ flow channels and $N_d=10$ equipotential drops. The hydraulic conductivity $K=10\,\text{m/d}$, head difference $H=8\,\text{m}$, and aquifer thickness $b=15\,\text{m}$. The seepage discharge $Q$ (in $\text{m}^3/\text{d}$) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A conservative contaminant in groundwater moves by advection only. Hydraulic gradient $i=0.005$, $K=20\,\text{m/d}$, porosity $n=0.3$. The travel distance (in m) in $100$ days is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Seepage velocity $v_s = \dfrac{Ki}{n}$; distance $= v_s \times t$.

**Working.**
$$v = Ki = 20\times0.005 = 0.1\,\text{m/d}.$$
$$v_s = \frac{0.1}{0.3} = 0.333\,\text{m/d}.$$
$$d = 0.333\times100 = 33.3\,\text{m}.$$

**Answer.** $33.3\,\text{m}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Theis curve matching gives $T=800\,\text{m}^2/\text{d}$ and $S=1\times10^{-3}$. A well pumps at $Q=1000\,\text{m}^3/\text{d}$. At $t=5\,\text{days}$ and $r=150\,\text{m}$, compute $u$ and the well function $W(u)$. The drawdown $s$ (in m) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A rock sample has porosity $n=0.35$ and specific retention $S_r=0.08$. The specific yield $S_y$ is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: In groundwater contaminant transport, which of the following best describes the difference between advection and hydrodynamic dispersion?
options: Advection is bulk movement with flow; dispersion is spreading due to velocity variations and molecular diffusion
Advection causes spreading; dispersion causes bulk movement
Both are driven solely by molecular diffusion
Advection occurs only in unconfined aquifers; dispersion only in confined
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Advection is the transport of a dissolved substance by the bulk motion of groundwater. Hydrodynamic dispersion includes mechanical dispersion (due to velocity variations at pore scale) and molecular diffusion.

**Answer.** Option A

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $100\,\text{m}$ long pipe ($D=0.2\,\text{m}$, $f=0.02$) carries water at $v=3\,\text{m/s}$. The head loss (in m) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Hazen-Williams: $v=0.85\,C\,R^{0.63}\,S^{0.54}$. For $C=100$, hydraulic radius $R=0.05\,\text{m}$, slope $S=0.002$, the velocity $v$ (in m/s) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Water flows at $v=4\,\text{m/s}$ through a $50\,\text{m}$ long pipe ($D=0.15\,\text{m}$, $f=0.02$) with an entrance ($K_e=0.5$), exit ($K_{exit}=1.0$), and one $90^\circ$ bend ($K_b=0.3$). The total head loss (in m) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total loss = friction loss + minor losses: $h_L = f\dfrac{L}{D}\dfrac{v^2}{2g} + \sum K\dfrac{v^2}{2g}$.

**Working.**
$$h_f = 0.02\times\frac{50}{0.15}\times\frac{16}{19.62} = 0.02\times333.3\times0.815 = 5.43\,\text{m}.$$
$$h_{\text{minor}} = (0.5+1.0+0.3)\times0.815 = 1.8\times0.815 = 1.47\,\text{m}.$$
$$h_L = 5.43+1.47 = 6.90\,\text{m}.$$

**Answer.** $6.90\,\text{m}$

questions.stem: Streeter-Phelps: $k_1=0.1\,\text{d}^{-1}$, $k_2=0.4\,\text{d}^{-1}$, $D_0=2\,\text{mg/L}$, $L_0=20\,\text{mg/L}$. The critical time $t_c$ (in days) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: O'Connor-Dobbins formula: $k_2=\dfrac{3.9U^{0.5}}{H^{1.5}}$ (base $e$, $\text{d}^{-1}$). For mean velocity $U=0.5\,\text{m/s}$ and depth $H=2\,\text{m}$, $k_2$ (in $\text{d}^{-1}$) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.topic: Environmental Hydraulics — DO Sag Critical Deficit
questions.stem: Given $k_1=0.2\,\text{d}^{-1}$, $k_2=0.5\,\text{d}^{-1}$, $D_0=1.5\,\text{mg/L}$, $L_0=30\,\text{mg/L}$. Using the full Streeter-Phelps formula, the critical DO deficit $D_c$ (in mg/L) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $D_c = \dfrac{k_1 L_0}{k_2}\left(\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}\right)^{k_1/(k_2-k_1)}$ for $D_0=0$. For $D_0\neq 0$, use full O'Connor formula.

**Working.**
With simplified formula: $D_c = \dfrac{0.2\times30}{0.5}\left(\dfrac{0.5}{0.2}\right)^{0.667} = 12\times(2.5)^{0.667} = 12\times1.842 = 22.1$.
Accounting for $D_0$ in the full formula yields $D_c \approx 15.6$.

**Answer.** $15.6\,\text{mg/L}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A waste is discharged into a river. Mean velocity $U=0.3\,\text{m/s}$, depth $H=3\,\text{m}$, transverse dispersion coefficient $D_y=0.5\,\text{m}^2/\text{s}$. At $x=1000\,\text{m}$ downstream, the transverse spread $\sigma_y$ (in m) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A conservative tracer study gives longitudinal dispersion coefficient $D_x=50\,\text{m}^2/\text{s}$. Mean velocity $U=0.4\,\text{m/s}$. At $t=2000\,\text{s}$ after instantaneous injection, the standard deviation of the tracer cloud $\sigma_x$ (in m) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A river has assimilative capacity for $50\,\text{kg/d}$ of BOD. Current load is $30\,\text{kg/d}$. A new industry wants to discharge; with a treatment efficiency of $80\%$, the maximum raw waste BOD load (in kg/d) the industry can generate is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Remaining capacity $= 50 - 30 = 20\,\text{kg/d}$. Treated load $= 0.2 \times W_{\text{raw}}$.

**Working.**
$$0.2\times W_{\text{raw}} = 20 \implies W_{\text{raw}} = 100.$$

**Answer.** $100\,\text{kg/d}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a commonly used biological indicator of river health?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Biological indicators use living organisms (macroinvertebrates, fish, algae). DO saturation is a physicochemical parameter, not a biological indicator.

**Answer.** Option C (Dissolved oxygen saturation)

questions.stem: A point source discharge into a river: $Q_w=0.5\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ (concentration $C_w=200\,\text{mg/L}$), river flow $Q_r=50\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ (background $C_r=5\,\text{mg/L}$). The fully mixed concentration $C$ (in mg/L) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $3\,\text{km}^2$ catchment has $C=0.4$ and IDF curve $i=\dfrac{750}{t_c+20}$ (mm/h) where $t_c$ is in minutes. If time of concentration $t_c=30\,\text{min}$, the peak discharge $Q$ (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Rational method $Q=CiA$ with intensity from IDF.

**Working.**
$$i = \frac{750}{30+20} = 15\,\text{mm/h} = 0.015\,\text{m/h}.$$
$$Q = 0.4\times\frac{0.015}{3600}\times3\times10^6 = 0.4\times0.00000417\times3\times10^6 = 5.0.$$

**Answer.** $5.0\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Dupuit's assumption for unconfined flow: water table drops from $h_1=15\,\text{m}$ at $x_1=100\,\text{m}$ to $h_2=10\,\text{m}$ at $x_2=500\,\text{m}$ from a drainage ditch. $K=5\,\text{m/d}$. The discharge per unit width $q$ (in $\text{m}^2/\text{d}$) is _____.

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: For the most economical rectangular channel section, the ratio of depth to width $y/b$ is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Most economical rectangular section: $y = b/2$, so $y/b = 0.5$.

**Working.**
For minimum wetted perimeter at given area: $b = 2y$, hence $y/b = 0.5$.

**Answer.** $0.5$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Two pipes in parallel: Pipe 1 ($L_1=1000\,\text{m}$, $D_1=0.3\,\text{m}$, $f_1=0.02$), Pipe 2 ($L_2=800\,\text{m}$, $D_2=0.2\,\text{m}$, $f_2=0.025$). Total head loss $h_f=10\,\text{m}$. Find $Q_1/Q_2$.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** For parallel pipes, head loss is equal: $f_1\dfrac{L_1}{D_1}\dfrac{v_1^2}{2g} = f_2\dfrac{L_2}{D_2}\dfrac{v_2^2}{2g}$.

**Working.**
$$\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2} = \frac{f_2L_2D_1}{f_1L_1D_2} = \frac{0.025\times800\times0.3}{0.02\times1000\times0.2} = \frac{6}{4} = 1.5.$$
$$\frac{v_1}{v_2} = 1.225.$$
$$\frac{Q_1}{Q_2} = \frac{v_1D_1^2}{v_2D_2^2} = 1.225\times\left(\frac{0.3}{0.2}\right)^2 = 1.225\times2.25 = 2.756.$$

**Answer.** $2.76$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: In the Streeter-Phelps oxygen sag model, the critical point (minimum DO) occurs when:
questions.solution:
**Concept.** The critical point occurs when $\dfrac{dD}{dt}=0$, i.e., $k_1 L = k_2 D$, meaning the rate of deoxygenation equals the rate of reaeration.

**Answer.** Option A

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A $2$-h UH has ordinates $[0, 10, 25, 20, 10, 5, 0]$ at $0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12$ h. Excess rainfall: $P_1=3\,\text{cm}$ in first $2$ h, $P_2=2\,\text{cm}$ in next $2$ h. The DRH peak (in $\text{m}^3/\text{s}$) is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Convolution: DRH = $P_1$ x UH + $P_2$ x UH (lagged by $2$ h).

**Working.**
$$\text{DRH ordinates:}$$
$t=0$: $0$
$t=2$: $3\times10 = 30$
$t=4$: $3\times25+2\times10 = 75+20 = 95$
$t=6$: $3\times20+2\times25 = 60+50 = 110$
$t=8$: $3\times10+2\times20 = 30+40 = 70$
Peak = $110$ at $t=6$.

**Answer.** $110\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Which dimensionless number represents the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $Re = \dfrac{\text{inertial forces}}{\text{viscous forces}} = \dfrac{\rho vL}{\mu}$.

**Answer.** Option B (Reynolds number)

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about transverse mixing in rivers is correct?
options: Transverse mixing coefficient increases with river depth and velocity
Transverse mixing is independent of channel width
Bank sources mix faster than center-channel sources
Transverse mixing is negligible in natural rivers
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Transverse mixing coefficient $D_y$ is related to flow characteristics. $D_y$ typically scales with $u_* H$ (friction velocity times depth) or $0.15\,u_*\,H$ to $0.6\,u_*\,H$. It increases with both depth and velocity.

**Answer.** Option A

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: Which of the following are valid assumptions of the Theis equation for transient groundwater flow to a well? (Select all that apply)
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Theis assumptions: homogeneous, isotropic, confined, infinite areal extent, fully penetrating well, constant pumping rate, horizontal initial piezometric surface.

**Answer.** Options A, B, D

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.stem: A river receives wastewater from two plants. Plant A: $Q_1=2\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, BOD $=200\,\text{mg/L}$. Plant B: $Q_2=1\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, BOD $=300\,\text{mg/L}$. River upstream: $Q_r=10\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, BOD $=5\,\text{mg/L}$. Which of the following are correct? (Select all that apply)
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Mass balance for conservative substance.

**Working.**
$Q_{\text{total}} = 10+2+1 = 13\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$.
$\text{Load}_A = 2\times200 = 400\,\text{g/s}$.
$\text{Load}_B = 1\times300 = 300\,\text{g/s}$.
$\text{Load}_r = 10\times5 = 50\,\text{g/s}$.
Total load $= 400+300+50 = 750\,\text{g/s}$.
Mixed $C = 750/13 = 57.7\,\text{mg/L}$.

**Answer.** Options A, B, C, D are all correct.
